interpretation: Outcome was structurally predictable. Pre-war factors (coalition air dominance, Iraqi logistics weakness, economic disparity, 35-nation alliance) overwhelmingly predicted coalition victory. The uncertainty was about casualties, not outcome.
pre_war_knowable_factors: Coalition air superiority, Iraqi air force weakness, poor NCO/officer corps, massive GDP/resource imbalance, sanctions damage, no replacement capacity, coalition naval/air deployment
surprise_factors: Duration and casualty count; chemical weapons threat; Iraqi Scud attacks on Israel

interpretation: Outcome was partially predictable from qualitative factors but the speed and totality of Israeli victory exceeded structural expectations. Pre-war analysis would note Israeli qualitative superiority and Arab coalition fragility but not predict 6-day resolution.
pre_war_knowable_factors: Israeli qualitative military superiority, Arab coalition political fragility, Israeli reserve mobilization capacity, US implicit support
surprise_factors: Speed and completeness of Arab air force destruction; collapse of Egyptian defenses in Sinai

interpretation: Balanced pre-war conditions produced genuine uncertainty. Structural factors (roughly balanced forces, complex alliances) largely captured the dynamics. The war's attritional character was not predictable from pre-war balance alone.
pre_war_knowable_factors: Roughly balanced forces, complex but known alliance structures, German mobilization speed advantage, industrial capacity roughly matched
surprise_factors: Schlieffen Plan failure; trench warfare stalemate; Ottoman entry; Russian collapse timing

interpretation: Pre-war structural assessment underestimates the decisiveness of Prussian victory. French political instability and Prussian military organization advantages were partially known, but the completeness of French collapse was not.
pre_war_knowable_factors: Prussian military organization advantage, French political instability after Second Empire, Prussian rail mobilization system
surprise_factors: Speed of French collapse; Sedan encirclement; Paris siege duration

interpretation: Structure predicted decisive UN advantage, but Chinese intervention transformed the war into stalemate. The most analytically interesting negative delta: structural factors overpredicted decisiveness.
pre_war_knowable_factors: UN/US material superiority, North Korean economic weakness, South Korean geographic position
surprise_factors: Chinese intervention; MacArthur's Inchon landing; Pusan perimeter survival

interpretation: The extreme negative delta case. US material superiority was overwhelming on paper, but North Vietnamese political will, guerrilla warfare strategy, and US domestic political constraints transformed a structural advantage into prolonged attrition.
pre_war_knowable_factors: US material superiority (GDP, industrial capacity, military size), South Vietnamese territorial control, Alliance support
surprise_factors: North Vietnamese political will persistence; guerrilla warfare effectiveness; US domestic opposition; Tet Offensive psychological impact

interpretation: Near-balanced pre-war conditions produced genuine uncertainty. Neither side had decisive structural advantage. The war's attritional character was predictable from the balanced starting position.
pre_war_knowable_factors: Near-balanced military forces, comparable economic capacity, both sides had motivated populations
surprise_factors: Iranian human wave tactics; Iraqi chemical weapons use; stalemate dynamics

interpretation: Allied material superiority was moderate. Multi-front war complexity not captured by simple ratios. The outcome was roughly predictable from structure, with the material balance slightly favoring the Allies.
pre_war_knowable_factors: Allied economic and industrial superiority, multi-front war pressure on Axis, Soviet manpower depth
surprise_factors: German tactical proficiency; Japanese naval capability; atomic bombs; D-Day timing
